The sha256 is computed on this device the moment the image is picked; the profile carries only that hash — the image body never goes online.
The image body never goes online; there is no cropping and no re-encoding today.
“Save profile” writes the profile fields; the picked image does not sync with the profile yet (see below).

This is what the page actually does today: pick an image, hash it, save the profile fields — all on this device. Cross-device sync of the image itself (cropping, re-encoding, on-demand fetch) is not implemented yet; that is the goal, not the current state.
Saved; the profile rev is now v%1$d. The picked image is not saved with the profile yet.
Only these 64 hex digits go over the wire

The image body never goes online; only this one hash travels with the profile. The peer sends avatar{op:"get"} on demand to fetch it — the images nobody could keep up with on a LAN never enter anyone’s bandwidth. The 32 KiB limit serves the same purpose: keeping the base64 envelope safely below one TCP control frame (64 KiB).
Saving works, but this image doesn't sync yet

Custom avatar exchange (the av1 capability) requires on-demand fetch, caching, and framed chunk transfer. The current version prioritizes instant synchronization via preset avatars and initials; custom avatar network roaming will be enabled in a future release.

Tray residency and background behaviour. These settings only affect this computer and are never synced to the other side — which is why they live under "This computer", a group that is not drawn on mobile.

Once tucked into the tray, heartbeats and scans slow down 3× (heartbeat %1$ds → %2$ds, offline detection %3$ds → %4$ds). The cost is that others see you come online later — and you find peers later too.
Start Tidings in the background at login (tucked into the tray, no window). Off by default — with it off, messages from others wait until you open the app by hand.
